key_insight: SwarmLink enables UAVs to coordinate directly with each other so photovoltaic inspection missions can keep working despite link loss, drone failure, or unusable imagery.
engineering_relevance: This matters for solar-plant inspection because it removes the ground station as a single point of failure and preserves full coverage with minimal changes to an existing aerial software stack.
method: Adds peer-to-peer communication on top of existing UAV frameworks without modifying the host system
Uses a distributed auction to assign sensing targets at mission start and to reassign them after failures or bad-quality captures
Re-auctions remaining targets among active drones for all disruption cases, including platform loss and degraded data
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a photovoltaic plant inspection case study in which the approach was integrated with Aerostack2 and used to unify allocation, failure recovery, and quality-based reassignment at runtime.
watch_item: The abstract does not provide quantitative performance results, so the operational overhead and scalability of the re-auction mechanism remain to be validated experimentally.
paper_title: Distributed Coordination for Resilient Multi-UAV Remote Sensing: A Photovoltaic Inspection Case Study
